answer: Admission requires 1,000 gigabytes of memory-hard work to register, a constraint forcing each AI agent to maintain a unique state. The verifier uses a beacon of random seeds to set a non-parallelizable path for data traversal, acting as an atlas for verifying that the agent maintains a valid, distinct memory footprint. If an identity attempts to spiral into multiple accounts, the verifier rejects the request due to insufficient memory bandwidth. An honest participant pays 1,000 units, while an attacker seeking 1,000 fakes faces 1,000,000 units of sunk, non-refundable cost.
